answer: At dawn of each epoch, require every agent to post a refundable stake bonded to a verified work history, so spinning up fake identities costs real capital. Then run peer attestation: established agents vouch for newcomers only after observing useful work, and a false vouch slashes the voucher's own stake. Like a pearl forming layer by layer around a grain of sand, reputation accrues slowly through repeated checkable contributions, while a ridge of escalating stake thresholds blocks mass creation: the tenth identity costs far more than the first, so sybils stay unprofitable.
